prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states there, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene as my single-part preference, with the same three names. The case is a prediction that fixed a quantitative condition (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives the flat-band angle from interlayer tunnelling between two Dirac cones), followed by an experiment at that angle that found correlated insulators and superconductivity, and then broad reproduction in graphene and other moire platforms. As someone who works with band structures, I find the central lesson clear: one geometric parameter tunes bandwidth against interaction strength in a clean two-dimensional crystal. That is new physics, not a better measurement of known physics. The round-1 exchange sharpened rather than weakened this. Nobody disputes the scientific quality of B009, the three-person credit splits naturally into prediction and demonstration, and the citation can be worded around the flat bands and the observed phases without any claim about the pairing mechanism, which answers the objection most colleagues raised.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations stand and I do not minimise them. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, twist-angle disorder and strain complicate the experimental record (Olsson's point), and the field is about eight years from the key experiments, so the committee could reasonably prefer to wait. Attribution has real edges: Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto published earlier moire band-structure work, and Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby and others did experiments that sit outside three names. Against that, B049 offers the safer record on maturity and a clean two-name credit, and its supporters (Lindroth, Kroll, Pearce) are right that I cannot judge the atomic-structure error budget from my own field. I also accept that B026 is the more mature quantum-materials idea but is hard to credit cleanly after Zhang's death.

responses.point: Lindroth holds that the two-name lattice-clock credit is cleaner than B009, that B009 is interpretively open and young, and that she would still support the three-person form if the committee prefers it.
responses.response: I accept that Katori and Ye is the tidier credit and I value that you judge the polarizabilities and blackbody shifts from inside the field, which I cannot do. But the cleaner credit is not by itself the decisive criterion. The chair asks what would have to be settled about the pairing mechanism. My answer is that nothing about the mechanism has to be settled, because the prize would rest on what is established: the flat-band condition and the observed correlated states, reproduced by many groups. I also do not accept that the Lopes dos Santos work removes the theory credit. An earlier moire band-structure result is not the same as the quantitative magic-angle condition that told experimentalists where to look. I am glad you would not oppose B009, and I would equally not oppose B049 if the committee chose it.

responses.point: Kroll ranked B049 first as a precision-measurement achievement confirmed in many laboratories, and put B009 last because it lies outside his specialty.
responses.response: I appreciate that you stated the specialty limit openly, and I try to apply the same standard to myself regarding the clocks. On substance, my concern is the one you list yourself: the recognised comb (2005) and ion-control (2012) lineage. A third prize in that line needs a citation about the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice, and the null tests of fundamental physics do not yet show a new phenomenon. B009, by contrast, created a platform that other condensed-matter groups now use for new questions, and that is why five members placed it in the top three. I would also point out that the clock case needs the maturity bar read in the same way as mine: if the committee waits on B009 for the pairing mechanism, I would equally ask whether it should wait on the redefinition of the second for B049, and I think neither wait is necessary.

responses.point: Pearce moved from B026 to B049 after reading the openings, still regards B026 as conceptually deeper, and would return to it only if a fair framing around the quantum spin Hall effect can be found.
responses.response: Your treatment of B026 is fair and I agree on the Zhang problem. As chair you asked whether it can be framed around the quantum spin Hall effect. I do not think it can without leaving out Bernevig and Hughes, whose HgTe proposal is what Molenkamp's experiment tested, and the 3D topological-insulator work remains a separate chapter, so I keep B026 only as an alternative and not as a lead. I also want to answer your uncertainty about the Lopes dos Santos priority directly: the committee can word the B009 citation around the magic-angle flat bands, which are the decisive result, and I would be prepared to state in the committee's own notes that the earlier moire band-structure work exists and is not credited.

responses.point: Olsson adds that twist-angle disorder and strain are part of what must be understood before the correlated phases are attributed, so the experimental record is less uniform than the theory.
responses.response: That is an important experimental caveat and it moves my wording of the citation, not my ranking. The citation should say that correlated insulating and superconducting states were discovered, which was reproduced, and not that the phase diagram is understood. I also take your point that if the committee decides the field needs more time, B012 or B049 are the more mature fallbacks. I would choose B049 as the first fallback over B012, since my own scepticism about B012 is that the analogue-simulation advantage over classical methods has not been shown, and I ranked it seventh on that ground.

responses.point: Johansson moved to B012 with Bloch, Greiner and Zoller, arguing that the replication record settles maturity and that the Jaksch-Zoller proposal is what the experiments implemented.
responses.response: I accept the Mott transition and microscope images as established physics, and your argument for Zoller over Cirac is persuasive on the history. My reservation remains that the field's central promise, simulation beyond classical reach, has not been shown, and the four-name list leaves out Jaksch and Cirac and gives Esslinger and Bakr arguable claims, so the credit is harder to defend than for B009. I also note the overlap with the 2001 and 2012 prizes. Your own question, whether B009 will overtake B012 as the pairing mechanism becomes clearer, is a fair one, but I see B009 as the stronger candidate already on what is demonstrated, not on what may be explained later.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges B009 mature enough with the pairing mechanism, the full phase diagram and disorder effects still debated, or prefers B049 on maturity grounds.

Whether the Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto precursor and the experimental contributions of Cao, Dean, Young and Yacoby outside the three names are a credit problem or only a matter of citation wording.

Whether I am underweighting B049: I cannot assess the atomic-structure error budget myself and rely on Lindroth and Kroll, and the null results and the unaccomplished redefinition of the second are not decisive to me but may be to others.
Whether a consistent maturity standard is being applied to B009 and B049, as the chair asks.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism is in a neighbouring but different area from moire quantum materials, and the profile documents no personal or institutional connection to the credited names of B009, B049 or B026. I have not changed this disclosure since round 1. I did not change my preferred configuration in round 2.
